prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form that made incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange my preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part B034 prize to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The chair is right that round 1 settled merit and maturity and left only framing and the third name open, so I will argue those directly. The chain from proglucagon processing, to the active GLP-1(7-36) amide, to the incretin effect and receptor biology, to outcome-trial evidence in glycaemic, weight, cardiovascular and renal endpoints is original, mature and independently confirmed. Framing the prize around the physiology and active form of the hormone is the most defensible reading of the prize tradition, because it rewards the discovery that made the drugs possible without turning the citation into a verdict on any one product. The five-to-one split on the third name is not a reason to follow the majority; I hold Mojsov because the identification and synthesis of the active peptide is an upstream discovery step on which both the physiology and the later analogue design depend.
statement.case_against: The weakness remains attribution. Habener's group disputes priority for the active form and is not among the credited names. Any three-name cut also omits Knudsen, whose analogue design is what reached patients, and a discovery-framed prize will be read by some as passing over the step that made the medicine. I cannot settle the Mojsov-Habener question from the supplied record, and I will not claim to. If the committee concludes that the priority claim for the active peptide cannot be sustained on the primary record, B034 with Knudsen in place of Mojsov would then be my fallback, not a move to a different candidate. A single-part prize also forgoes the clean two-person attribution available for B003, which is a real if smaller cost.

responses.point: The chair proposes Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, with a citation covering physiology and the development of long-acting therapies, accepting that this honours industrial development and is the less conservative choice if the committee wants a discovery-only framing.
responses.response: I agree with the chair's candour that the Knudsen configuration is a different framing and not a better-evidenced attribution of the same one. Your citation is coherent, and the long-acting analogues are what generated the outcome data that make the timing right. But my own round-1 test was that the framing should be fixed before the names, and I fix it on discovery. On that reading Mojsov's identification of the active peptide precedes and enables the engineering Knudsen did. I would change to your configuration only if the primary record showed Mojsov's claim is not sustainable, not because naming a company scientist is more convenient or because the controversy is public. I would also ask that the final citation wording acknowledge therapy so that the omission of Knudsen is not read as a judgement on her work.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius rests the case on a basic-discoverer trio and states that if the active-peptide priority could not be assigned cleanly, a B034 prize would be fragile and B003 would be the safer alternative.
responses.response: I share your concern that the Mojsov question is the point where the prize could crack, but I do not accept that it makes B003 the safer alternative. If the priority record were against Mojsov, the physiology contributions of Drucker and Holst and the translational work of Knudsen would still stand, so B034 would survive with a different third name rather than collapse. B003 is a very clean Walter and Mori pair, which is why I keep it as my first alternative, but its human therapeutic validation is thin and it would be a retreat from the stronger medical case, not a repair of this one. I would only go to B003 if no three-name B034 configuration could command a majority.

responses.point: Perlmann treats B003 as the cleaner fallback with a clear two-person attribution and a very mature basic discovery, though with less direct clinical impact, and notes the PERK and ATF6 branches may be hard to separate from the core story.
responses.response: I agree on the clean Walter and Mori attribution and on the maturity of B003, and my view of the integrated stress response matches yours: it blurs the boundary of the core discovery, so a citation would need to be drawn carefully around IRE1 and XBP1 signalling. I still think a single-part B034 is better than pairing it with B003. A two-part prize would cut the GLP-1 credit to two names and would remove either Mojsov or the third discoverer, which is the dispute we are trying to avoid, and it would pair a very large clinical achievement with one whose medical translation is still partial. I would revisit only if the committee finds B034 cannot be credited with three names.

responses.point: Linnarsson says the committee should decide whether the prize rewards physiology or therapy, that the names follow from that, and that omitting Knudsen risks reading as rewarding hormone biology while skipping the people who made it a drug.
responses.response: I agree that the framing decides the names and that the committee should settle it first. Where I would go further than your round-1 note is on the cost of the discovery framing. It is a real cost that Knudsen is omitted, so the citation should say explicitly that the discoveries made incretin-based therapies possible. The three-name limit and the priority of discovery are the reasons for the omission, and those reasons are principled. I do not think leaving a fourth name out undermines the prize, because the citation names the therapy even when the laureates are the discoverers.

responses.point: Sandberg supports the Drucker, Holst and Mojsov trio and argues that Knudsen should not be dismissed as merely industrial, so the citation should acknowledge translation to therapy and the reason for exclusion should be the three-person limit.
responses.response: I agree with that. The omission of Knudsen should be justified by the three-person cap and by the priority of discovery in the citation, not by the industrial setting of her work. I am also glad that you take the outcome trials as the evidence that makes the timing right and not as the object of the prize. On that point I would keep the citation as I have drafted it, naming the therapies as what the discoveries made possible.

uncertainties: Whether the primary record supports Mojsov's priority for the active peptide form against Habener's group, and whether Habener's omission should change the configuration. I cannot settle this from the supplied evidence.
Whether the committee settles the framing as discovery physiology or discovery plus therapy before choosing the third name, since I treat that framing as deciding Mojsov or Knudsen.

Whether B003 or B040 is the better second choice if B034 does not reach four votes on one exact three-name set, and whether the Eshhar and other chimeric-receptor originator omissions can be resolved for B040.
Whether long-term safety questions for incretin therapy could affect the maturity assessment; I currently think they do not.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal need applies to any shortlisted candidate. My documented collaborations with Grillner, Ernfors and a 2009 paper with Perlmann concern motor, pain and stem-cell neuroscience and involve no one credited on the shortlist, and none of the round-1 exchange changes that.
